why: Swelling in the dilute beaker and shrinking in the concentrated one places the raisin cell sap between the two, which is statement (ii), and the option carrying the text (B) is option B.
solution: Raisins swelled in beaker A, so water moved into them, which means their cell sap is more concentrated than the dilute solution A. Raisins shrank in beaker B, so water moved out of them, which means the very concentrated solution B is stronger than the cell sap. Together these place the sugar concentration of the raisins above that of solution A and below that of solution B, which is statement (ii). Nothing that was observed points to a damaged membrane or to any change in the permeability of the membrane. Matches option B.

why: NCERT states that the pore opens when water flows into the guard cells and swells them, and closes when the guard cells shrink.
solution: The stomatal pore is bounded by two guard cells, and it is their water content that opens and closes it. When water flows into the guard cells they swell, their curved shape pulls the pore open, and when water leaves them they shrink and the pore closes. Temperature and oxygen have no direct role in this mechanism, and the loss of water through the pore is the reason a plant closes its stomata when it does not need carbon dioxide. Matches option B.

why: Only the star-shaped region received light, so only there was starch made, and starch gives a blue-black colour with iodine.
solution: Iodine turns blue-black only where starch is present, and a destarched leaf can form starch only in the parts that receive light. Light reached the leaf solely through the star-shaped hole cut in the black paper, so photosynthesis and starch formation were confined to that star. The star therefore turns blue-black, while the region that stayed covered has no starch and keeps the plain brown colour of the iodine solution. Matches option D.

why: A hypertonic solution is more concentrated than the cell sap, so water leaves the cell by osmosis.
solution: A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the contents of the cell, so water diffuses down its own concentration gradient from inside the cell into the surrounding solution. The cell consequently loses water and shrinks, which in a plant cell is seen as plasmolysis. Water enters a cell only when the outside solution is hypotonic, and there is no net movement in either direction only when the solution is isotonic. Matches option B.

why: Amylase occurs both as salivary amylase and as pancreatic amylase, and amylase acts on starch, a carbohydrate.
solution: Saliva contains salivary amylase and pancreatic juice contains pancreatic amylase, and both of these break starch down into simpler sugars. Starch is a carbohydrate, so carbohydrate is the food component attacked in the mouth and then again in the small intestine by the same kind of enzyme. Proteins are handled by pepsin in the stomach and trypsin in the pancreatic juice, and fats by bile salts and lipase, none of which is present in saliva; minerals need no digestion at all. Matches option C.

why: By definition a heterotroph cannot make its own food and depends on food made by other organisms.
solution: Autotrophs build their own food from carbon dioxide and water using the energy of sunlight, whereas heterotrophs lack this ability and must take in food that other organisms have already made. The three rejected statements all describe autotrophic nutrition, since converting carbon dioxide and water into carbohydrates and using solar energy for photosynthesis are exactly what an autotroph does. Matches option A.

why: Statements (ii) and (iv) describe the true routes; (i) swaps the atria and (iii) invents a left atrium to right ventricle connection.
solution: Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium, passes into the right ventricle and is pumped to the lungs, while oxygenated blood returns from the lungs into the left atrium, passes into the left ventricle and is pumped to the whole body. Statements (ii) and (iv) each state a part of this correctly. Statement (i) is wrong because it swaps the two atria, and statement (iii) is wrong because the left atrium opens only into the left ventricle, the two sides of the heart being kept completely separate so that oxygenated and deoxygenated blood do not mix. Matches option A.

why: Balance and precision of learned movement belong to the cerebellum, which lies in the hind brain, so row (c) is the correct pairing.
solution: Maintaining posture and balance, and the precision of a learned movement such as riding a bicycle or walking in a straight line, are the work of the cerebellum, and the cerebellum is a part of the hind brain. The cerebrum of the fore brain deals with thinking and voluntary decisions, and the medulla of the hind brain controls involuntary actions such as heartbeat, blood pressure and vomiting. Only row (c) pairs the hind brain with the cerebellum. Matches option B.

why: Olfactory receptors, the receptors for smell, lie in the lining of the nose.
solution: Smell is a chemical sense, and the olfactory receptors that detect chemicals carried in the air are located in the lining of the nasal cavity. The tongue carries the gustatory receptors that give the sense of taste, the inner ear carries receptors for sound and for balance, and the skin carries receptors for touch, pressure, pain and temperature. Matches option B.

why: Thyroxine is an iodine-containing hormone, which is why iodised salt prevents goitre.
solution: The thyroid gland needs iodine to manufacture the hormone thyroxine, which regulates the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats in the body. If iodine is short in the diet the gland cannot make enough thyroxine and it enlarges, producing the swelling called goitre, and this is the reason common salt is iodised. Insulin and adrenaline are built from other materials and need no iodine, and auxin is a plant growth hormone rather than a human one. Matches option A.

why: The bud stays attached and separates only when fully mature, so the claim that it leaves the parent as soon as it is produced is the untrue one.
solution: In Hydra a bud arises as an outgrowth formed by repeated cell division at one particular site on the body, and it remains attached while it grows its own mouth and tentacles. It separates from the parent only when it is fully mature, after which it lives as a new independent individual. The statement that it leaves the parent body as soon as it is produced therefore contradicts what actually happens, while the other three statements are all true of budding. Matches option A.

why: Only strip Q became longer, and a strip gains water and lengthens only when the surrounding liquid is more dilute than the cell sap, which is true of pure water.
solution: A potato strip in pure water absorbs water by osmosis, its cells become turgid and the strip gets longer. Strip Q is the only one that grew, from 78 mm to 80 mm, so liquid Q is the water. Liquid P left its strip unchanged, so that sugar solution was isotonic with the cell sap, while liquids R and S shortened their strips because those solutions were more concentrated than the cell sap and drew water out of the cells. Matches option A.

why: Membrane biogenesis is a function of the endoplasmic reticulum, and the rough endoplasmic reticulum is the only ER offered, though strictly the lipid half of the job belongs to the smooth ER.
solution: Membrane biogenesis is a function of the endoplasmic reticulum: ribosomes studding the rough endoplasmic reticulum manufacture proteins, and lipids are made by the smooth part of the same network, and some of these proteins and lipids go into building the cell membrane. Mitochondria release energy rather than build membranes, the Golgi apparatus only modifies, packages and dispatches material that has already been made in the endoplasmic reticulum, and the plasma membrane is the product here and not the maker. Of the four choices only the rough endoplasmic reticulum belongs to this manufacturing system. Matches option C.

why: The kitchen of the cell is the chloroplast, and only the oval organelle with stacks of thylakoids is a chloroplast.
solution: Food is manufactured by photosynthesis in the chloroplast, the green plastid that holds chlorophyll, which is why the chloroplast is called the kitchen of the cell. The diagram to choose is therefore the oval organelle whose interior contains stacks of disc-shaped thylakoids, since the chlorophyll sits in those thylakoid membranes. The lobed bean-shaped body is a mitochondrion, which is the powerhouse rather than the kitchen, and the stack of curved sacs with budding vesicles is the Golgi apparatus. Matches option D.

why: The graph shows contraction rate rising as osmolarity falls, and a more dilute solution drives more water in by osmosis, so more bailing out is needed.
solution: The contractile vacuole exists to expel water that has entered the cell by osmosis, so the rate at which it contracts must track the rate at which water enters. A solution of low osmolarity is more dilute than the cell contents, so water floods in faster and the vacuole has to empty more often, which is precisely the rise seen as osmolarity falls along the graph. Option B fails because an isotonic point is not marked and would in any case only stop the net movement of water, option C invokes salt entering the cell, which the graph does not measure and which would if anything raise water uptake, and option D assumes a fall in respiration for which there is no evidence at all. Matches option A.

why: Mitochondria self-replicate, the nerve cell is the longest human cell, chromoplasts are the coloured plastids and chromatin is the threadlike nuclear material.
solution: Mitochondria carry their own DNA and their own ribosomes and can make some of their own proteins, so they are able to make more of themselves and are the self-replicating organelle, giving (a) to (iv). The nerve cell or neuron is the longest cell in the human body, giving (b) to (i). Plastids that carry pigments other than the green chlorophyll are chromoplasts, giving (c) to (iii), and the threadlike material inside the nucleus that condenses into chromosomes at cell division is chromatin, giving (d) to (ii). Matches option D.

why: Air is trapped when the coverslip lands all at once, so it must be lowered gently.
solution: Bubbles form when the coverslip meets the mounting fluid all at once and traps air beneath it, so it must be lowered slowly and gently, ideally at an angle with the help of a needle, so that the liquid spreads ahead of the advancing edge of the glass. Dropping the coverslip from a height is the surest way to trap air, and letting the peel fold over itself leaves pockets of air under the fold. Leaving the peel in stain for over an hour affects only how darkly it stains and has nothing to do with bubbles. Matches option A.

why: Cardiac muscle is the only branched involuntary muscle, and it is found in the heart.
solution: Cardiac muscle is the only muscle in the body that is both branched and involuntary; its fibres are cylindrical, have a single nucleus, branch and join with neighbouring fibres, and contract rhythmically without rest throughout life. Such muscle occurs only in the wall of the heart. The muscle of the ureters is smooth and involuntary but is spindle-shaped and unbranched, while the muscle of the limbs and of the tongue is striated and under voluntary control. Matches option C.

why: Tracheids lose their contents and die at maturity; sieve tubes, companion cells and parenchyma are all living.
solution: Tracheids are xylem elements that lose their cell contents at maturity and die, leaving only their thick lignified walls, and it is this hollow dead tube that lets water move up the plant without obstruction. Sieve tubes are living even though they lose their nucleus, and they depend on the living companion cells beside them to keep working. Parenchyma is a living packing tissue with thin walls and intercellular spaces. Matches option B.

why: Apical and intercalary meristems are meristematic, that is dividing, tissues and are the opposite of permanent tissue.
solution: Meristematic tissue is defined by its ability to divide, and apical, intercalary and lateral meristems are its three kinds, so calling apical and intercalary meristems permanent tissues is the incorrect sentence. Permanent tissue is what meristematic cells become once they have lost the power to divide and have taken a fixed shape and function. The other three sentences are all correct: young meristematic cells are packed with dense cytoplasm and lack vacuoles, collenchyma is thickened irregularly at the corners of its cells, and parenchyma does have intercellular spaces. Matches option A.

why: Long cylindrical fibres with alternating light and dark bands are the definition of striated muscle.
solution: Alternating light and dark bands along a long cylindrical fibre are exactly what gives striated muscle its name, and this muscle is also called skeletal or voluntary muscle because it moves the bones under conscious control. Smooth muscle cells are spindle-shaped, taper at both ends and show no banding at all. Parenchyma is a plant tissue and would not appear as banded fibres, and a neuron has a cell body with long branching processes rather than any striation. Matches option B.

why: P and Q are growing follicles, which secrete oestrogen, and oestrogen thickens the endometrium, so statement (iv) alone is correct.
solution: P and Q are follicles at successive stages of growth, and a growing follicle secretes oestrogen, whose task is to thicken the endometrial lining of the uterus so that it is ready to receive an embryo, which makes statement (iv) correct. Statement (i) fails because ovulation does not occur before puberty, so no released ovum T exists then. Statement (ii) fails because the progesterone secreted by the corpus luteum R suppresses rather than stimulates the release of luteinising hormone, and statement (iii) fails because S is the corpus albicans, the degenerated remnant of the corpus luteum, which secretes no hormone. Matches option A.

why: Rapid spread needs numerous spores plus a moist nutrient-rich surface on which they can germinate.
solution: Bread mould spreads quickly because it releases very large numbers of light spores that settle over the whole slice, and because moist bread supplies both the water and the nutrients those spores need in order to germinate at once. Branched tubular hyphae and round sporangia are structural features of the mould itself; they explain how the fungus absorbs food and how it produces spores, but they are not what makes the spread across a slice of bread so rapid. Matches option B.

why: The voice cracks when the larynx enlarges under testosterone, which is a secondary sexual characteristic of boys.
solution: At puberty the larynx of a boy enlarges under the influence of testosterone, and while it is growing the voice breaks and cracks before settling into a deeper adult pitch, so this change is tied specifically to sexual maturation. An increase in height and a gain in weight occur in both sexes and also during ordinary childhood growth, so neither marks sexual maturation. The milk teeth are shed several years before puberty begins. Matches option B.

why: Both an Amoeba daughter cell and a yeast bud are smaller than the parent, which is statement (i), and the option carrying the text (A) is option B.
solution: In binary fission an Amoeba divides into two daughter cells, so each daughter begins life smaller than the parent that produced it. In budding a small outgrowth appears on the surface of the yeast cell and enlarges gradually, so the bud too is smaller than its parent while it is attached. The first statement records both of these correctly, whereas the remaining statements claim equal or larger daughter cells, which no dividing or budding cell can produce from a fixed amount of parent material. Matches option B.

why: The ten per cent law gives two tenfold steps between the producer and the third trophic level, so 50 kJ becomes 5000 kJ.
solution: Only about ten per cent of the energy held at one trophic level is passed on to the next, the rest being lost as heat and in life processes, so the energy falls by a factor of ten at every step. The third trophic level is two steps above the producers, so it holds one hundredth of the producer energy. Working backwards from 50 kJ, one step gives 500 kJ at the herbivore level and a second step gives 5000 kJ at the producer level. Matches option A.

why: Tree is producer, grasshopper herbivore, frog secondary consumer, snake secondary carnivore, giving 1-A, 2-C, 3-B, 4-D.
solution: A tree makes its own food by photosynthesis and so is the producer, giving (1) to (A). The grasshopper feeds on the plant and is therefore a herbivore or first-order consumer, giving (2) to (C). The frog eats the grasshopper and so stands at the third trophic level as the secondary consumer, giving (3) to (B), and the snake, which eats the frog, is the flesh eater one step further along and is the secondary carnivore, giving (4) to (D). Matches option C.

why: The 1987 UNEP agreement froze CFC production because CFCs were destroying the ozone layer.
solution: Chlorofluorocarbons, used in refrigerators and in fire extinguishers, were found to be breaking down the ozone layer that shields the earth from ultraviolet radiation. In 1987 the United Nations Environment Programme succeeded in forging an agreement to freeze the production of these compounds at their existing levels and then to cut them back. Carbon dioxide emissions, water pollution and the conservation of biodiversity are the subjects of other, separate international agreements. Matches option C.

why: Ozone is a poison and is formed by ultraviolet light splitting oxygen molecules, while the shielding is against ultraviolet, not infrared, and ground-level ozone is harmful.
solution: Ozone is chemically a deadly poison at the level at which we breathe, so the first statement is true, and high in the atmosphere it is formed when ultraviolet radiation splits oxygen molecules into free oxygen atoms that then combine with other oxygen molecules, so the third statement is true as well. The second statement is wrong because the ozone layer screens out ultraviolet radiation and not infrared, and the fourth is wrong because ozone performs its essential shielding function only in the upper atmosphere, while at ground level it acts as a harmful pollutant. Matches option D.
